# `scikitplot.impute`

<!-- Generated by `python tools/maint_tools/generate_usage_skills.py sync` from the installed package; edit the module's docstrings or `__all__`, not this file. -->

Transformers for missing value imputation.

## Install

```sh
pip install scikit-plots
```

The release on PyPI can be older than the version this skill was read from, and
can lack `scikitplot.impute`. If `import scikitplot.impute` fails after
installing it, the installed release predates the module: the [release history
on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/scikit-plots/#history) lists each release,
and [pip's user guide](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/) explains
upgrading.

## Read the API of the installed version

The table below was read from one version of scikit-plots; the project may
have another, and the installed package decides. Check the version, then read
what it declares (shown for `MissingIndicator`; use the name you need):

```sh
python -c "import scikitplot; print(scikitplot.__version__)"
python -m scikitplot api scikitplot.impute
python -c "import scikitplot.impute as m; print(m.__all__)"
python -c "import scikitplot.impute as m; help(m.MissingIndicator)"
python -c "import inspect, scikitplot.impute as m; print(inspect.signature(m.MissingIndicator))"
```

- `python -m scikitplot api` lists every public name with its kind, signature
  and summary (`--name NAME` for one in full, `--format json` for tools).
  Releases before it report an error instead (an unknown command, or a
  missing dependency of an older command line): then use the next lines,
  which work on every release.
- `__all__` is the public list; `help()` is the full documentation of one name,
  methods included; `inspect.signature` is its exact call signature.
- Both read the installed objects. If they ever differ, `help()` and
  `inspect.signature` are the source of truth.

## Example (from the docstring of `scikitplot.impute.ANNImputer`)

```python
import numpy as np
from scikitplot.experimental import enable_aknn_imputer
from scikitplot.impute import ANNImputer
X = np.array([[1, 2, np.nan], [3, 4, 3], [np.nan, 6, 5], [8, 8, 7]])
# imputer = ANNImputer(backend="voyager", n_neighbors=5, metric="euclidean")
imputer = ANNImputer(n_trees=5, n_neighbors=5)
imputer.fit_transform(X)
# array([[1. , 2. , 5. ],
#        [3. , 4. , 3. ],
#        [4. , 6. , 5. ],
#        [8. , 8. , 7. ]])
```
